title: X0 hardware gate (Qwen3.6-27B, 2x H100 box): does the new box reproduce one 23 Oct necessity cell?
command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py parts --name x0_hw_gate_parts_27b --map d1_topics2_map_27b --why "X0 hardware gate: one 23 Oct cell (bridge_word:16) rerun on the 2x H100 box" --lo 16 --sets bridge_word --force bridge_word:16 && uv run python scripts/x0_hw_gate.py --new x0_hw_gate_parts_27b --ref d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2 --cell bridge_word:16
question: Does the new box (2x H100 80GB PCIe, x86_64, driver CUDA 12.8) reproduce, read for read, a cell the 23 Oct necessity run (d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2, A100) measured: the bridge's word at layer 16, both readers, the same scenes, map, lens and code path?
why_it_matters: X0 compares its numbers with the 23 Oct ones and is the gate for the week. A hardware or kernel difference that flips reads would be confounded with the effect.

hypotheses.H-same: the reads agree on >= 97% of rows without random draws. Prior: none set (an agreement check, not a claim)
hypotheses.H-differs: the agreement is below 97%: X0 does not start; the disagreeing rows are reported

decision_rule: Fixed 24 Oct before the run (hardware addendum v2: "rerun one 23 Oct cell, item agreement at least 97%"). Rows are matched on item, set, layer, part, source and null flag (scripts/x0_hw_gate.py). The gate covers the rows whose arm draws no random tensor: full, lens2, not_lens2, jspace, not_jspace, jspace_wo_own and not_jspace_matched, non-null, both readers. PASS iff the share of those rows whose read role (b / A / other) matches the 23 Oct row is >= 0.97. Otherwise FAIL: the script exits 3, so the X0 jobs that depend on this one do not start. Arms drawing random tensors (rand_omp, rand_sub, not_rand_sub, the matched pieces, every null; drawn on CUDA in this code) are reported per part, not gated. The median |ld| difference is reported per group.
controls: the reference run itself: the same code path (statement_positions.py, exp04_brew_parts.py, suite_split.py, tasks_v2.py, suite_v1.py and src/bridge_jspace/ have no diff between c2e31c9, the reference run's commit, and this commit)
the random-draw arms reported beside the gate
n: 180 scenes x 2 readers (PP, PM) of d1_topics_v2, one cell (bridge_word:16), 7784 rows in the reference
notes: The reference ran on the A100 box at c2e31c9 (dirty tree; the parts code path has no diff since). Inputs are committed: results/statement_positions/d1_topics2_map_27b, results/tasks_v2/d1_topics2_competence_27b, results/statement_positions/d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2. GPU0, first job of the queue (hardware addendum v2). Timing basis: the reference's 8 cells took ~1.3 h on one A100; one cell is ~10 min.

question: At the 27B's layer 32, at the asked person's bridge word in the org run (chat), split by whether the bridge's locker sentence comes before or after the asked pick sentence: can a linear probe read (a) the lookup's answer digit, (b) the index of the sentence holding the bridge's locker, (c) the bridge's identity (positive control), above the majority and chance baselines?
why_it_matters: X0 says the 27B and 9B lookups flip mostly in locker-before scenes and do not need the J++ part (9B) or need more atoms of it (27B); the digit check found no digit route. The probes ask what the word holds instead: the answer value itself, or an address of where it is.

hypotheses.H-value: (a) high in locker-before and at chance in locker-after: the answer value is stored at the word, not in J++ form. Prior: none set (descriptive, after data; Dan's reading)
hypotheses.H-address: (b) high in locker-before with (a) at chance: the word stores an address (a lookback-style pointer). Prior: none set (Dan's reading)

decision_rule: Descriptive, added after data, not part of X0's rule (Dan, 24 Oct evening). Linear probes (one-hot ridge, standardized features, penalty by inner 4-fold CV) on h_org at the bridge's word, layer 32; (a) and (b) cross-validated by bridge entity (5 folds, entities held out), (c) by item (5 folds, entities spread: a held-out entity is an unseen class). Per target and stratum (locker before / after / both): accuracy against chance (1 / classes) and the training folds' majority class; for (b) also the structure-only baseline (the agent's addition: the most frequent locker index given the asked pick's sentence index). 95% CIs from a cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000 resamples, seed 0); probe - best baseline on the same draws. Primary: the 200 X0 items of x0_necessity_27b_chat; secondary: every chat scene of d1_topics_v3. Reading (Dan, before the run): (a) high before and at chance after -> value at the word; (b) high before with (a) at chance -> address.
controls: locker-after scenes: the locker sentence follows the word, so (a) and (b) cannot be read from it there (control by construction)
the bridge identity probe (positive control: the pipeline reads what the word surely holds)
majority-class and chance baselines, cross-validated; the structure-only baseline for (b)
n: 200 X0 items (101 locker-before, 99 locker-after; 38 / 33 entities) and every chat scene of d1_topics_v3 (600)
notes: Order (Dan, 24 Oct evening): after the single-change alt, before the 122B. Cost: one model load, 600 forwards (~10 min). States saved fp16 in results (states.npz, ~6 MB), so further probes are CPU-only.

question: On the single-change items (x0_single_27b_r2 at L32, qwen35_9b_x0_single_r2 at L12; locker-before primary), with P the probe-(b) subspace (the decision directions of a linear probe for the index of the bridge's locker sentence, fit on fresh d1_topics_v4 org states, locker-before; rank = classes - 1): (1) does removing PΔ from the bridge edit cost the lookup more flips than removing a random part of the same share, while the recall loses no more than with the random part? (2) does PΔ alone flip the lookup more than the random part alone?
why_it_matters: The probe reads the address (which sentence holds the bridge's locker) at the bridge's word in locker-before scenes, and not the answer digit. If the lookup acts on the bridge through that address, removing it should cost the lookup, not the recall; keeping only it should carry the lookup's flips. Expected direction (Dan): the lookup loses flips, the recall does not.

hypotheses.H-lookup: lookup: probe dependence - random dependence > 0 (lower CI > 0), locker-before. Prior: Dan's, predictions batch 27
hypotheses.H-recall: recall: probe dependence - random dependence <= 0.10. Prior: Dan's, batch 27
hypotheses.H-sufficiency: lookup: S_probe_only / S_whole - S_rand_only / S_whole > 0 (lower CI > 0). Prior: Dan's, batch 27

decision_rule: Descriptive, added after data (Dan, 24 Oct ~18:45, item 6). Per model, reader and locker order: S for whole, no_probe (Δ - PΔ), no_rand (Δ minus X0's random-subspace part at PΔ's share), probe_only (PΔ), rand_only (the random part alone, the agent's matched control); probe dependence 1 - S_no_probe / S_whole against the random one (excess, paired), and S_probe_only / S_whole against S_rand_only / S_whole (paired); 95% CIs from a cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000 resamples, seed 0); top-token read, both readers on the identical patch. Locker-before is primary; locker-after descriptive (lookups rarely flip there). Results not opened or summarized before Dan's batch-27 commit.
controls: the random-subspace part at PΔ's share (removal) and the random part alone (sufficiency)
both readers on the identical patch
the probe trained on fresh scenes (d1_topics_v4), disjoint from the test items (d1_topics_v3)
n: the 200 single-change items per model (~100 locker-before)
notes: One 2-GPU job, two processes (27B on GPU0, 9B on GPU1). Depends on x0_probe_power (its states train P). The run also saves h_org, Δ and the J++ parts of Δ at k = 25 and 100 per item (states.npz), for Dan's items 2 and 3 (the probe on h_alt and on patched states, CPU). Cost: 200 items x 6 reads x 2 readers + OMP at k = 100: ~15 min per model.

question: On the single-change items (x0_single_27b_r2 at L32, qwen35_9b_x0_single_r2 at L12), both readers: how many flips are lost when Δ loses (w) its least-squares fit on the J++ directions of the org and alt bridge tokens and their one-token surface variants, (jw) its 25-atom J++ part with those variants banned, (pca) its 25-atom part over the top 2,000 principal directions of the layer (200 held-out d1_topics_v4 prompts, every token), and (jpp) X0's J++ part, each against a random part of its own share?
why_it_matters: The J++ part is mostly not the bridge word (the bridge's tokens are in the top 25 atoms of 28 of 40 items, ~12% of the part), so "the bridge's word form" is not shown. This separates the word from J++ beyond the word, and J++ from any direction the layer favours.

hypotheses.H-word: recall's loss mostly in w. Prior: Dan's, predictions batch 27
hypotheses.H-beyond: recall's loss mostly in jw, with pca inert. Prior: Dan's, batch 27
hypotheses.H-geometry: pca about as large as jpp for recall. Prior: Dan's, batch 27

decision_rule: Descriptive, added after data (Dan's audit, 24 Oct ~19:30, item 2). Per model, reader and part: median share of ||Δ||², S_whole, S_no, S_noRand, Jdep, Rdep, excess (X0's cells; cluster bootstrap over bridge entities, 10,000 resamples, seed 0), top-token read, both readers on the identical patch. Reading (Dan): recall's loss mostly in w -> the word form; mostly in jw with pca inert -> J-space beyond the word; pca about as large as J++ -> "J++-specific" means "aligned with the layer's geometry", and the README must say so. title: Batch 45, 45b on the 9B (L12): where is the binding made when the locker comes after the pick? Bridge-word change at L, L/2, L/4; S patched into O at the locker sentences at L and L/2
command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= uv run python scripts/x45b_binding.py run --name qwen35_9b_x45b_binding --why "batch 45, test 45b (jobs/c3/batch45.yaml): the 9B at L12; (a) the bridge-word change at L, (b) at L/2 and L/4, (c) S patched into O at every locker-sentence token at L, (d) at L/2; S read on S"
examples_command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b uv run python scripts/x45b_binding.py examples --name qwen35_9b_x45b_binding
question: In the main test's scenes where the original bridge's locker sentence comes after the asked pick, is the binding made at the locker sentences rather than at the bridge word: does patching S's states into O at every token of the locker sentences (at L or L/2) switch at least half of the lookups that S itself switches, while the bridge-word change at L switches at most 0.25?
why_it_matters: In these scenes the bridge-word change switches few lookups (x0_strata, 24 Oct: 0.19 on the 9B at L12, 0.09 on the 27B at L32, against 0.86 / 0.76 where the locker comes first), although S itself switches them all. If the model can only bind the pick to its locker once it reads the locker sentence, the change lives at the locker sentences, and the lookup's low rate there is about reading order, not about the bridge word.

hypotheses.Q45.5: The reading-order explanation holds: (a) yes; (b) no. Dan's answer in docs/predictions_batch45.md (Q45.5), committed before any result of this test is opened.

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (batch 45, jobs/c3/batch45.yaml, 45b): the reading-order explanation holds if (c) or (d) switches at least half of the lookups that S itself switches, while (a) stays at or below 0.25. As implemented (scripts/x45b_binding.py, rule): the lookup, point estimates; "half of the lookups S switches" = among the items whose lookup S read on S switches, the share (c) (or (d)) switches >= 0.5; (a) = its switch rate over all the items <= 0.25; can't tell if S switches none. Switch = the top token at the read step is S's answer's first token (X0's chat read). Rates with cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge items (10,000 resamples, seed 0) and the n.
controls: (a) the bridge-word change at L: the main test's whole arm rerun on these items (stored 0.19 on the 9B, x0_strata); checked against the stored reads of qwen35_9b_x0_necessity (a at L12, b_half at L6)
S read on S: what S itself switches (the rule's reference); checked against the stored S read (competence.jsonl)
O unedited (arm none): reads O's answer
the recall read on the identical patches (descriptive)
n: the 100 items of qwen35_9b_x0_necessity (chat, L12) whose org locker sentence comes after the asked pick, 28 bridge entities; all 100 align token for token between O and S (plan stage, 26 Oct)
notes: Results stay closed until docs/predictions_batch45.md holds Dan's Q45.5 commit: the job runs the run and examples stages only; the verdict after that commit, on the CPU: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b uv run python scripts/x45b_binding.py verdict --name qwen35_9b_x45b_binding. Locker sentences = every 'The locker of <thing> is <n>.' sentence of the context (3 per scene; one that comes before the first changed pick has h_S = h_O, a no-op). L/2 = 6, L/4 = 3. est_gpu_hours from the timing ledger (H100 PCIe): qwen35_9b_x0_single_r2 took 612 s for about ten times this run's forwards (competence on 600 scenes and 8 layers of reads), qwen35_9b_x0_probe 87 s (load and a few hundred forwards); this run: 100 items x (2 recorded forwards + 2 readers x (one 6-row read of O + one read of S)) + 10 example items' greedy tokens, about 3 minutes.

As computed (x6_routes.first_locker_rule): the lookup's position share with only the pointer part (keep_alf) on the C2 scenes whose pointer move (the O bridge's locker slot -> the S bridge's) involves slot 0, the base scenes every variant has (paired); a variant cuts if its point estimate is <= 0.5 x V0's and the paired cluster-bootstrap 95% CI of V0 minus it has lower bound > 0; within = |variant - V0| <= 0.10 on the point estimates; if both rules hold (possible when V0 <= 0.2) the first is reported and flagged; a variant that misses its gate makes the verdict "not tested". decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch45.yaml, 45k, with its overrides). "Identity route is lens-readable on the 27B" if on the 27B, from k = 25 to k = 100, identity answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, while position answers fall by less than 0.1 (or rise); and on the 9B neither falls by at least 0.1. "Pointer becomes lens-readable on the 27B" if position answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, and the k = 100 span's mean cos^2 with U is at least 0.5. "Generic fitting" if jpp_other at k = 100 costs the 27B lookup at least 2/3 of what this scene's J++ costs (override 2: read on the main test, job x45k_generic_27b against results/x0_necessity/x0_kmatch_27b; the routes jpp_other arm in this job is descriptive). Otherwise "can't tell". Report all four per model. As computed (fixed before the run): "fall from k = 25 to k = 100 by at least x more than with the random part" = [share(no_jpp25) - share(no_jpp100)] - [share(no_jpp25_rand) - share(no_jpp100_rand)] >= x, C2 lookup route shares, point estimates (paired cluster-bootstrap CIs beside them); "position falls by less than 0.1 (or rises)" = the same difference for position < 0.1; the 9B clause: both identity's and position's difference < 0.1. Mean cos^2 with U = per C2 item ||P_span(atoms) U||_F^2 / rank(U), averaged over the items; with the identity direction, ||P_span(atoms) u||^2 / ||u||^2. "Costs the lookup" = the lookup's extra loss (switches lost without the part minus without its random part, over the whole change's switches). Each label is evaluated per model. Overrides (Dan ~22:05): 1. precondition: the 27B's C0 lookup extra loss at k = 100 (no_jpp100 vs its random part) is reported; below 0.2, Q45.9 is "can't tell: the main-test curve does not reproduce in routes scenes", whatever the other clauses say; 3. precedence for Q45.9: "Generic fitting" if it holds, otherwise the labels that hold on the 27B, otherwise "can't tell". Code: x6_routes.jppk_rule per run, jppk-summary over the runs (x6_routes.jppk_labels; generic_rule on the main test). no_jpp25 is the existing no_jpp arm (signed OMP, k = 25); thresholds with a 1e-9 tolerance (a value exactly at a bar counts as at it). Gates as the routes test (read accuracy 0.80; C0 within 0.10 of the 9B's reference). Cluster bootstrap over the bridge item, 10,000 resamples, seed 0.

title: Batch 45k on Muse L26 (if time): why does the lookup lose with more J++ atoms? The sanity swap (C0) and another item moved (C2) with J++ removed at 25, 50 and 100 atoms and another scene's 100 atoms refit here, each against a random part of its share; the atoms' overlap with the pointer and the identity direction
command: BJ_TARGET=muse-glimmer-30b BJ_DEVICE_MAP= uv run python scripts/x6_routes.py run --name muse30b_x6_routes_x45k_r3 --conditions C0,C2 --jpp-ks 25 50 100 --jpp-other --c0-min 0.5
question: On the 27B the main test's lookup extra loss grows with the J++ atoms (0.12 / 0.30 / 0.60 at k = 25 / 50 / 100; about 0 on the other models). Do the extra atoms take out the identity route, the pointer, or any fitted directions?
why_it_matters: The 9B's J++ part at k = 100 holds more of the change (44%) than the 27B's (31%), so "removed too much" does not explain the curve. Which route the lookup loses as k grows, and how much the k atoms overlap the pointer and the identity direction, tell a lens-readable route from overfitting.

hypotheses.H-batch45: Q45.9 (45k) in predictions/2026-10-26_dan.md (section Batch 45), committed by Dan before any 45k code or run (8025b808); overrides (Dan ~22:05) committed before any 45k job (1fad1c34)

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch45.yaml, 45k, with its overrides). "Identity route is lens-readable on the 27B" if on the 27B, from k = 25 to k = 100, identity answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, while position answers fall by less than 0.1 (or rise); and on the 9B neither falls by at least 0.1. "Pointer becomes lens-readable on the 27B" if position answers in C2 fall by at least 0.2 more than with the random part, and the k = 100 span's mean cos^2 with U is at least 0.5. "Generic fitting" if jpp_other at k = 100 costs the 27B lookup at least 2/3 of what this scene's J++ costs (override 2: read on the main test, job x45k_generic_27b against results/x0_necessity/x0_kmatch_27b; the routes jpp_other arm in this job is descriptive). Otherwise "can't tell". Report all four per model. As computed (fixed before the run): "fall from k = 25 to k = 100 by at least x more than with the random part" = [share(no_jpp25) - share(no_jpp100)] - [share(no_jpp25_rand) - share(no_jpp100_rand)] >= x, C2 lookup route shares, point estimates (paired cluster-bootstrap CIs beside them); "position falls by less than 0.1 (or rises)" = the same difference for position < 0.1; the 9B clause: both identity's and position's difference < 0.1.
